name: ar-puuk/overture-data-download
what_it_holds: R + DuckDB script to download Overture Maps Foundation data (places/buildings/etc.) for a given area of interest.
why_useful: R-based alternative acquisition method for the same hotel-POI source; only useful if the team's pipeline is R rather than Python.
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: R-based alternative acquisition method for the same hotel-POI source; only useful if the team's pipeline is R rather than Python.

name: arthurgailes/overtureR
what_it_holds: R package that loads Overture Maps datasets as dbplyr/sf-ready data frames (21 stars), i.e. an R client library for the same places/hotel POI data.
why_useful: Makes the Overture places (hotel/lodging) pull scriptable and joinable in R for anyone building the hotel-supply proxy in R rather than Python/DuckDB directly.
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: Makes the Overture places (hotel/lodging) pull scriptable and joinable in R for anyone building the hotel-supply proxy in R rather than Python/DuckDB directly.

name: whubsch/overturetoosm
what_it_holds: Python package translating Overture Maps schema/tags to OpenStreetMap tags (and vice versa conceptually), useful for cross-walking Overture's accommodation categories to OSM's tourism=hotel/motel/hostel/guest_house tagging scheme.
why_useful: Lets a hotel-supply build reconcile counts pulled from Overture with counts pulled directly from OSM (Overpass/Geofabrik extracts), giving two independent POI sources to cross-check a hotel-count time series.
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Lets a hotel-supply build reconcile counts pulled from Overture with counts pulled directly from OSM (Overpass/Geofabrik extracts), giving two independent POI sources to cross-check a hotel-count time series.

Enables cross-walking Overture Places categories to OSM tourism=* tags (and vice versa) so a lodging-supply count built from one source can be reconciled/merged with the other, improving coverage and cross-validation.

name: OvertureMaps/explore-site
what_it_holds: Interactive web map for exploring Overture Maps data themes (including places/accommodation) release-by-release; points at the same S3/Azure-hosted Parquet releases as OvertureMaps/data, useful only for eyeballing coverage before committing to a bulk pull.
why_useful: Quick visual QA of hotel POI density/coverage in specific ABNB markets before investing in the DuckDB pull.
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: Quick visual QA of hotel POI density/coverage in specific ABNB markets before investing in the DuckDB pull.

name: WhereInTheWorldIsWikipedia
what_it_holds: Wikimedia Research team code for geographically mapping Wikimedia pageviews (i.e. attributing pageviews to reader geography/country), not article-topic geography.
why_useful: Marginal: could in principle help split 'reader interest by country' for a destination article, which is a weaker but distinct signal (who is searching about a place) versus 'interest in a place.' Not a ready dataset.
time_coverage: unspecified, likely historical Wikimedia research-era (repo appears older/low-activity)
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Marginal: could in principle help split 'reader interest by country' for a destination article, which is a weaker but distinct signal (who is searching about a place) versus 'interest in a place.' Not a ready dataset.
